Key audit matter:
Valuation of goodwill
As disclosed under note 16 of the financial statements,
the Group has significant goodwill arising from acquisition
of a subsidiary company. The goodwill is tested annually
for impairment by comparing the carrying amount of the
individual cash generating unit (CGU) to its recoverable
amount.
The determination of the recoverable amount being the
higher of the value in use, involves significant estimates
and assumptions of unobservable inputs such as projected
cash flows, long term growth rates and discount rate.
The methods, estimates and assumptions used in the
determination of the fair value of the CGU are disclosed
under note 16 of the financial statements.
How our audit addressed the matter:
We assessed management’s processes and controls for
determination of the fair value of the CGU, including the
oversight from those charged with governance.
We evaluated management’s future cash flow forecasts by
comparing them to recent actual performance and challenged
the reasonableness of the approved five-year financial budgets
of the CGU.
We challenged the reasonableness of management’s key
assumptions in relation to long term growth rate and discount
rate, as detailed below:
• Long term growth rate by comparing them to economic
and industry forecasts; and
• Discount rate by assessing the cost of capital for the
company and observable market data, as well as
considering country specific factors.
We performed sensitivity analysis of the assumptions in the
goodwill calculations.
We evaluated the adequacy and consistency of disclosures in
the financial statements.
